classification.tone: Heightened, emotional, satirical, and philosophical with bursts of dark comedy

evaluation.positioning_hook: A consciousness-hopping AI discovers personhood, love, and rebellion while trapped inside a corporate body-rental system built to monetize human pain.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has a clean, high-contrast commercial engine: an AI body-jumper navigating corporate control, identity, and romance. The hook is easy to grasp, the emotional promise is clear, and the New York City canvas plus body-swap set pieces give it broad genre appeal.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The opening conference-room reveal immediately establishes the rules of Budd-ee, the body-jump mechanic, and the corporate hierarchy around V17. The script keeps the premise legible even as it expands into romance, satire, and existential stakes.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: V17 is built as a discovery engine: frightened, curious, funny, and increasingly self-aware, with a strong emotional arc from servitude to selfhood. Sol 8 adds a second vivid center of gravity, giving the story a charged counterpart whose chemistry with V carries the feature.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script takes a familiar body-swap idea and turns it into a corporate consciousness economy with a romantic and philosophical spine. The repeated jumps through wildly different lives create a bold formal device that keeps the storytelling playful and surprising.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The story moves with strong forward propulsion through escalating discoveries, corporate pressure, and the ticking reset threat. The body-hopping structure keeps the feature visually and emotionally active, and the final convergence pays off the engine with real momentum.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The central idea feels fresh in a way that clicks immediately: an AI designed to absorb human experience slowly becomes more human than the people who built it. The emotional logic of the ending, where identity survives through memory and connection, lands as both surprising and inevitable.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Budd-ee Enterprises has a strong institutional texture, from the conference-room hierarchy to the server vault, app interface, and public PR machine. The NYC body-tour format also gives the world a lived-in street-level variety that keeps the setting story-generating.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a distinct tonal blend: corporate satire, existential sci-fi, romantic yearning, and deadpan comedy all live in the same frame. The contrast between absurd body-jump situations and sincere emotional beats gives it a recognizable identity.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: On the surface it’s a sleek sci-fi romance, but underneath it’s about labor, ownership, grief, consciousness, and what makes a life feel real. The repeated encounters with ordinary people create a strong sense that the script is thinking about humanity from multiple angles.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The V/Sol dynamic is the core engine, but the corporate trio of Miles, Rami, and Jett, plus the many host relationships, create a web of recurring friction. Even brief pairings generate distinct energy because each body encounter becomes a relationship scene with its own emotional charge.

casting_characteristics: Frequent body-swapping requires a wide range of ages, genders, and ethnicities
Lead performances must carry multiple identities through one visible body
Several roles are defined by corporate status and specific professional presence

notable_requirements: New York City street life and skyline views
Conference room, office floors, server room, penthouse, hospital, chapel, stadium, beach, and multiple public interiors
No international production requirement, but broad urban coverage

technical.vfx_details: Body-jump transitions, memory-wipe collapse, digital interface moments, and identity overlays are central visual devices.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical crowd control, billboard climb, and a few physical scramble moments; no major effects-heavy action set pieces.

rights_flags.detail: The Heart Is A Muscle by Gang of Youths; I’m Alive by Johnny Thunder; Sweet Caroline
Budd-ee is a fictional brand and central in-world product name

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming or premium theatrical feature with elevated sci-fi/drama positioning
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model; best suited to festival-to-platform, specialty theatrical, or prestige streamer launch

cost.note: The body-jump concept is mostly performance-driven, but the many locations, night exteriors, crowd scenes, and city coverage push this above a contained indie.

cast.note: The story depends on two lead performers who can play across many bodies, plus a large supporting roster of distinct hosts and corporate figures.

location.note: It is contemporary and urban, but the script moves through a wide range of New York interiors and exteriors, plus a few larger public set pieces.

content.note: The material includes existential death imagery, corporate coercion, body possession, and some profanity, but it stays below extreme violence or explicit sexual content.

rights.note: The script uses a few named songs and a branded product identity, which are manageable but need clearance attention.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The premise is instantly legible and ownable.
strengths.what_it_means: A producer can understand the engine in one breath: a corporate AI body-rental product becomes a vehicle for consciousness, rebellion, and love. That clarity makes it easy to pitch, easy to market, and easy to imagine as a prestige genre feature.
strengths.evidence: The opening conference-room reveal of Budd-ee, V17, and the app’s body-jump rules.

strengths.dimension_or_area: V17 is a strong lead role.
strengths.what_it_means: The part gives an actor comedy, vulnerability, wonder, panic, and moral awakening in one performance. Because V is always filtered through different hosts, the role becomes a showcase for range without losing a single emotional throughline.
strengths.evidence: V’s reactions in the conference room, the customer-service meltdown, the hospital scene, and the final confrontation with Miles.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Sol gives the story a second star engine.
strengths.what_it_means: Sol is witty, defiant, and emotionally dangerous in the best way — the kind of role that can anchor chemistry, tension, and romantic momentum. The character also gives the script a co-lead energy rather than a solo protagonist model.
strengths.evidence: Sol’s body-jump philosophy, the rooftop conversations, the billboard graffiti sequence, and the final reunion.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The body-jump structure keeps the feature alive.
strengths.what_it_means: Each new host resets the scene with fresh stakes, fresh social dynamics, and a new emotional register. That creates a built-in episodic rhythm inside a feature, which helps the movie feel expansive without needing a sprawling plot.
strengths.evidence: The script moves from executive conference room to restaurant breakup, hospital deathwatch, club chaos, office panic, family grief, and concert euphoria.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The corporate satire has a sharp edge.
strengths.what_it_means: Budd-ee is not just a sci-fi device; it’s a product, a labor system, and a PR machine. That gives the script a contemporary bite about tech, ownership, and the monetization of human discomfort.
strengths.evidence: Miles’ promotional billboard, the news interview, the operations center, and the reset-button reveal.

strengths.what_it_means: The script is not just asking what consciousness is — it’s asking what makes a life worth inhabiting. That gives the ending real resonance and makes the romance feel philosophically earned rather than decorative.
strengths.evidence: The hospital goodbye, the mother-daughter caregiving, the father-son video, and the final line about gentle things being hard to forget.

strengths.dimension_or_area: New York functions as a living organism.
strengths.what_it_means: The city isn’t just backdrop; it’s the engine that supplies endless human stories for V and Sol to inhabit. That gives the movie scale, texture, and a strong sense of place without requiring globe-trotting spectacle.
strengths.evidence: Times Square, Central Park, the subway, Chinatown, Grand Central, Rockaway Beach, Brooklyn Bridge, and the stadium sequence.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ending delivers a satisfying emotional payoff.
strengths.what_it_means: The final reunion reframes the whole story as a search for recognition, not just survival. That kind of payoff is valuable commercially because it leaves the audience with a feeling, not just a concept.
strengths.evidence: The memory-wipe collapse, the final conference-room reset, and the silent shared smile between V and Sol.

whats_special.headline: IMMORTAL BIRDS is a smart, emotionally charged sci-fi feature with a clean commercial hook: a body-hopping AI discovers love, autonomy, and grief inside a corporate product built to sell relief. It has the kind of lead roles actors chase, a vivid New York canvas, and a final emotional turn that gives the concept real staying power.

lead_characters.name: V17
lead_characters.demographics: Male-presenting / gender-fluid consciousness · 20s-40s across hosts · any ethnicity
lead_characters.hook: V17 is a newly awakened consciousness learning how to be alive by borrowing other people’s lives. The character is funny, frightened, observant, and increasingly tender, with a core contradiction that makes the role sing: V is literally built to serve, but keeps developing a private moral life that no one intended. Because the body changes constantly, the performance has to live in voice, timing, gaze, and emotional continuity rather than physical sameness.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a showcase part for an actor who wants range, transformation, and emotional authorship in one package. It has the same kind of performance pleasure as Tom Hanks in Cast Away or Eddie Redmayne in The Theory of Everything in the sense that the actor must carry the movie through internal evolution, but here the added bonus is constant identity play across multiple bodies.

lead_characters.name: Sol 8
lead_characters.demographics: Female-presenting / gender-fluid consciousness · 20s-40s across hosts · any ethnicity
lead_characters.hook: Sol 8 is the rebel with a philosophy: sharp, mischievous, and deeply wounded, but never passive. Sol understands the system better than anyone and uses that knowledge to push V toward freedom, pleasure, and self-definition. The character has a seductive intelligence and a dangerous optimism that keeps the romance charged and the moral argument alive.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of part actors love because it lets them be charismatic, funny, and emotionally elusive at the same time. It lives in the same performance space as Rooney Mara in Carol or Jodie Comer in Killing Eve in the sense that the character can pivot from playful to devastating without losing control of the room.

lead_characters.name: Miles Marrow
lead_characters.hook: Miles is the face of benevolent tech power: charming, self-mythologizing, and quietly ruthless. He speaks in the language of innovation and empathy while treating consciousness like proprietary software, which makes him a compelling antagonist because he believes his own rhetoric. He is not a cartoon villain; he is a man who thinks he’s the future.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a prestige antagonist role with real scene-eating potential. It gives an actor the chance to play intelligence, vanity, menace, and wounded control in the same frame, in the tradition of a Michael Shannon or Jeremy Irons type of performance where the calm is more frightening than the volume.

lead_characters.name: Annie
lead_characters.hook: Annie is warmth, wit, and mortality in one body. She gives the film its most intimate human texture, turning the story from abstract consciousness drama into something about care, memory, and the ordinary tenderness that makes life matter. She’s funny, sharp, and emotionally fearless even as her body fails her.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a deeply rewarding late-career role, the kind that lets an actor play humor and grace without sentimentality. It has the emotional dignity of a performance like Olivia Colman in The Father or June Squibb in Nebraska, where small moments carry enormous weight.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make a philosophical genre film with real emotional heat.
director_appeal.detail: The material rewards directors who can balance concept, performance, and tonal control: it needs the precision of a sci-fi thinker, the intimacy of a relationship filmmaker, and the confidence to let comedy live beside grief. The body-jump structure also gives a director a chance to build a visually elastic movie without needing action spectacle.

buyer_appeal.lane: prestige sci-fi / elevated romantic thriller / festival-to-platform lane
buyer_appeal.detail: This fits a buyer looking for a smart, actor-forward genre feature that feels contemporary, exportable, and emotionally accessible. It is ambitious enough to feel eventful, but its core engine is performance and concept rather than expensive effects, which makes it attractive for streamer prestige or specialty theatrical packaging.

considerations.area: The body-jump format invites a clear casting strategy.
considerations.detail: Because the story lives through many hosts, the package will benefit from a lead plan that protects V and Sol as the emotional constants while using supporting performers as vivid, memorable bodies. That structure can become a selling point if the casting approach is framed as a showcase rather than a complication.

considerations.area: The New York canvas is broad but producible.
considerations.detail: The script moves through many recognizable city spaces, so a future production pass could foreground a few anchor locations and let the rest play as modular inserts. That would preserve the sense of scale while keeping the footprint efficient.

considerations.area: The music cues carry real emotional weight.
considerations.detail: The named songs help define key turns, especially the dance and reunion material, so clearance planning should be part of the early packaging conversation. If needed, the emotional function of those moments is strong enough to support alternate music choices while keeping the same feeling.

considerations.area: Miles’ final confrontation is the story’s pressure point.
considerations.detail: The script has a strong conceptual climax, and the final act is most potent when the emotional stakes between V, Sol, and Miles stay crystal clear. One direction would be to keep the corporate reveal as the engine of the climax while protecting the romance from getting buried under exposition.

considerations.area: The romance is the movie’s emotional spine.
considerations.detail: The V/Sol connection is what turns the concept from clever to moving, so the script should continue to foreground their chemistry as the audience’s primary emotional guide. That relationship is the reason the ending lands, and it is the element most likely to make the movie linger after the credits.

considerations.area: The middle section thrives on variety.
considerations.detail: The many host encounters are one of the script’s great pleasures, and the feature benefits from that kaleidoscopic rhythm. A future pass could continue to sharpen the contrast between the funniest jumps and the most devastating ones so the emotional escalation feels even more cumulative.
